concepts.def: A shaped piece of transparent material that forms an image by refracting light. The light changes direction as it enters the lens and again as it leaves, and that bending is what forms the image.
A lens that is thicker in the middle than at its edges. Rays of light arriving parallel to the principal axis are brought together to a focus at the principal focus.

A lens that is thinner in the middle than at its edges. Rays arriving parallel to the principal axis are spread apart, so that after the lens they appear to come from the principal focus on the same side as the object.
The straight line through the centre of the lens, at right angles to it, used as the reference line in every ray diagram.

The point on the principal axis at which rays of light that arrive parallel to that axis are brought to a focus by a convex lens. For a concave lens it is the point from which those rays appear to spread out.
The distance from the lens to the principal focus. It is a fixed property of a given lens: moving the object or the screen does not change it.
A drawing that uses straight lines with arrows to show the paths of selected rays of light, used to show how a lens forms an image and how large that image is.
An image formed where rays of light actually meet. Because the light really arrives there, a real image can be caught on a screen placed at that position.
An image formed where rays of light only appear to come from. The rays do not actually meet there, so no screen can catch it, but it can be seen by looking through the lens.

concepts.term: Image produced by a convex lens
concepts.def: It can be either real or virtual. With the object further from the lens than the principal focus the image is real and inverted; with the object nearer than the principal focus the image is virtual, upright and magnified.

concepts.term: Image produced by a concave lens
concepts.def: It is always virtual. Wherever the object is placed, the image is upright, smaller than the object and on the same side of the lens as the object.

concepts.term: Constructing a convex lens ray diagram
concepts.def: Two rays are enough. A ray from the top of the object parallel to the principal axis is refracted through the principal focus beyond the lens; a ray through the centre of the lens carries straight on. The top of the image is where they cross.

concepts.term: Constructing a concave lens ray diagram
concepts.def: A ray from the top of the object parallel to the principal axis is refracted so that it appears to come from the principal focus on the object side; a ray through the centre carries straight on. The image is found where the lines traced back cross.

How many times larger the image is than the object, calculated using magnification = (image height)/(object height). A value greater than 1 means the image is larger than the object; a value less than 1 means it is smaller.
Magnification is a ratio of two lengths, so the unit on the top cancels the unit on the bottom and the answer is a plain number with no unit attached.

concepts.term: Measuring image height and object height
concepts.def: Both heights should be measured in either mm or cm, and both must be in the same unit before they are divided, otherwise the ratio obtained is wrong.
In ray diagrams a convex lens is drawn as a vertical straight line with an arrowhead at each end pointing outwards, away from the principal axis.
In ray diagrams a concave lens is drawn as a vertical straight line with an arrowhead at each end pointing inwards, towards the principal axis.

mcqs.q: Rays of light travelling parallel to the principal axis pass into a convex lens. What happens to these rays?
options: They are refracted and brought to a focus at the principal focus
They are reflected from the front face of the lens to a point
They are refracted and cross each other at the focal length
They carry straight on because they meet the lens head-on
mcqs.explain: This is what the specification states: in a convex lens, parallel rays of light are brought to a focus at the principal focus.

mcqs.q: What is meant by the focal length of a convex lens?
options: The distance from the lens to the object being viewed
The distance from the lens to the principal focus
The distance from the lens to the sharp image
The thickness of the lens where it is widest
mcqs.explain: This is the specification's definition: the distance from the lens to the principal focus is called the focal length.

mcqs.q: A convex lens forms an image of a distant tree on a screen. Where does the light change direction?
options: Only at the surface where the light leaves the lens
At the shiny front face, where light is reflected
As it enters the lens and again as it leaves
Only at the middle, where it is thickest
mcqs.explain: A lens has two surfaces and refraction happens at both, which together bring the parallel rays from the tree to a focus.

mcqs.q: Which statement about the image formed by a concave lens is always true?
options: It is real if the object is far enough away
It is inverted, like the image from a lens
It is too faint for anyone to look at it
It is virtual, wherever the object is
mcqs.explain: The specification states that the image produced by a concave lens is always virtual, whatever the object distance.

mcqs.q: An object is placed between a convex lens and its principal focus, as in a magnifying glass. What sort of image is formed?
options: A real image, inverted and larger than the object
A virtual image, upright and larger than the object
A virtual image, upright but smaller than it
A real image formed at the principal focus
mcqs.explain: Inside the principal focus the rays leaving the lens are still diverging, so the image is virtual, upright and magnified.

mcqs.q: How can you tell that an image formed by a lens is real rather than virtual?
options: It appears the same way up as the object does
It can be seen by looking through the lens
It can be caught on a screen put where it forms
It is on the same side of the lens as the object
mcqs.explain: A real image is formed where rays of light actually meet, so a screen placed there shows it.

mcqs.q: In a ray diagram for a convex lens, how is the ray from the top of the object to the centre of the lens drawn?
options: It is bent so that it passes through the principal focus
It is curved to follow the two faces of the lens
It is bent back to run parallel to the principal axis
It carries straight on, with no change of direction
mcqs.explain: At the centre the faces of the lens are effectively parallel, so the ray emerges travelling in its original direction.

mcqs.q: In a ray diagram for a concave lens, a ray arrives parallel to the principal axis. How is it drawn after the lens?
options: Spreading away from the principal axis
Bending in to reach the principal focus beyond
Carrying straight on to the far side of it
Bending inwards to cross the principal axis
mcqs.explain: A concave lens diverges the light, and only the line traced backwards passes through the principal focus.

mcqs.q: A student draws ray diagrams for a convex lens and for a concave lens, using the same object in each. Which feature is the same in both diagrams?
options: Both images are the same way up as the object
Both images can be caught on a screen behind
The ray through the centre of the lens is undeviated
The parallel ray goes to the focus beyond the lens
mcqs.explain: This construction rule is shared by both lenses, and is one of the similarities a comparison of the diagrams should bring out.

mcqs.q: Which two quantities are needed to calculate the magnification produced by a lens?
options: The focal length of the lens and the object height
The distance to the image and to the object
The height of the image and the focal length
The height of the image and the object height
mcqs.explain: The specification gives magnification = (image height)/(object height), so the two heights are what is needed.

mcqs.q: An object 5 mm tall produces an image 15 mm tall. What is the magnification?
options: 3, from 15 mm divided by 5 mm
0.33, from 5 mm divided by 15 mm
3 mm, as the heights were in mm
10, from 15 mm minus 5 mm
mcqs.explain: magnification = (image height)/(object height) = 15/5 = 3, written as a plain number.

mcqs.q: An object 8.0 cm tall produces an image 2.4 cm tall. What is the magnification?
options: 3.3, since 8.0 is divided by 2.4
0.30, as the image is smaller
3.3, because a lens should enlarge
0.30 cm, from the heights in cm
mcqs.explain: magnification = (image height)/(object height) = 2.4/8.0 = 0.30, a value less than 1 because the image is diminished.

mcqs.q: A student measures both heights in centimetres and calculates a magnification of 2.5. How should this answer be written?
options: As 2.5 cm, keeping the unit of the heights measured
As 2.5 mm, since mm is a unit used for heights
As 2.5 m, because metres are the SI unit of length
As 2.5 on its own, because a ratio has no units at all
mcqs.explain: Magnification is a ratio and so has no units, so the answer is the bare number 2.5.

mcqs.q: An object is 4.0 cm tall and its image is 60 mm tall. What must be done before the magnification equation is used?
options: Convert one height so that both are in the same unit
Nothing at all, since a magnification has no unit anyway
Change both heights into metres before dividing
Divide the larger height by the smaller height
mcqs.explain: Image height and object height should both be measured in either mm or cm; here 4.0 cm becomes 40 mm, giving a magnification of 1.5.

mcqs.q: In ray diagrams, which symbol is used to represent a convex lens?
options: A vertical line with two arrowheads pointing inwards
A vertical line with outward arrowheads at each end
A shape drawn curved outwards on each of its two faces
A vertical line with one arrowhead at the top
mcqs.explain: The convex lens is drawn as a straight vertical line whose arrowheads point outwards, matching the outward bulge of the lens.

mcqs.q: Which symbol is used in a ray diagram to represent a concave lens?
options: A line with arrowheads pointing outwards at both ends
A line drawn thinner in the middle than at the edges
A line with inward arrowheads at both ends
A line with a single arrowhead at its top end
mcqs.explain: The concave lens is drawn as a straight vertical line whose arrowheads point inwards, towards the principal axis.
